inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($63M). NSC does not tag PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation separately; withholding is immaterial at SBC of 0.5% of revenue and is not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $534M (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); H1-2026 only $5M because the merger agreement restricts repurchases. The flat share count is a modelling convention funded historically (FY2021-22 $6.5B of buybacks) but currently suspended under the deal.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average Q2 2026 10-Q (225.0M; basic 224.5M, cover-page 224.6M at 2026-06-30); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.1% (10y UST), ERP 4.5%, beta ~1.1 (pre-deal rail beta; the merger-arb regime has collapsed observed beta and is not used) -> cost of equity ~9.1%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (BBB+/Baa1 curve), 21% tax -> 4.2% after tax. Market-value weights ~80% equity / 20% debt (market cap ~$70B vs $16.6B debt) -> WACC 8.0%. Same WACC on all three scenarios: cyclicality and deal-break risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases ($218M liability at FY2025; $92M/yr lease cost) are expensed inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already after the lease charge. Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B, charged once). Finance leases are immaterial. D&A used for cash-tax EBIT is the reported $1,393M, which carries no right-of-use depreciation of consequence.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest. Equity-method earnings (Conrail etc.) sit in other income and are left out of EBITDA; the stakes are not added to the bridge either, so nothing is counted twice.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income is not separately tagged after FY2017 (sits inside OtherNonoperatingIncomeExpense, $101M FY2025 net). Not stripped: NSC is net DEBT $15.5B, so the cash pile is not being added to EV and there is nothing to double-count.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes paid $491M against pre-tax income $3,665M (13.4%) and book tax $792M (21.6%); deferred tax expense $277M. Grossing the interest shield back onto the unlevered base gives ~15% on EBIT. Bonus depreciation (made permanent by the 2025 tax act) keeps the cash rate below book as long as capex exceeds D&A, which is structural for a railroad, so the ramp only goes to 19% not 21%.
inputs.debt_note: Q2 2026 10-Q: LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations $15,967M + current $649M = $16,616M (no current-portion double-count; the FY2025 DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations tag of $17,087M = 16,480 + 607 confirms the construction). Cash $1,069M. Net debt $15,547M.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md row: operating company, cyclical US industrial). Routed to owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (cyclical: risk charged once; leases: one treatment). Standalone Class I railroad valuation; the pending Union Pacific acquisition is NOT inside the three scenarios -- it is handled in deal_overlay and valuation_philosophy, because a stock-and-cash consideration is not a driver path. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $12,180M, GAAP OR 64.2% including East Palestine insurance recoveries; adjusted OR ~65-66%). Year-1 EBITDA margin (45.0%) is anchored to the H1-2026 adjusted run-rate (Q2 2026 adjusted OR 65.5%, GAAP 67.6% with merger costs; D&A ~10.5-11% of revenue), not to the recovery-flattered FY2025 47.2%. Year-1 owner FCF cross-check: engine ~$2.8B unlevered vs FY2025 actual OCF 4,361 + after-tax interest ~650 - capex 2,204 - SBC 63 = ~$2.74B. Price is a regular close, not after-hours. Band position: house and street IVs are ~$5 apart because SBC is 0.5% of revenue, and the price sits ~$150 above BOTH; the engine's band_position (~2,774%) is a degenerate reading of a tiny band, not a statement about SBC accounting -- the gap between price and both IVs is the merger premium plus the market's peer-multiple fallback, see deal_overlay.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, rounded down. Equity CAGR is unusable as the anchor: $6.5B of FY2021-22 buybacks and the FY2023 East Palestine charge ($1.1B pre-tax) drove book value, not earnings power. FCF CAGRs are flat because FY2020 was a capex trough (1,494) and FY2025 carries elevated capex plus settlement outflows.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 1.0% vs revenue 4.5% and EPS 10.1% (>30% divergence). Cause: buybacks (FY2021 $3.4B, FY2022 $3.1B) and the FY2023 derailment charge, not a shrinking business. EPS 5-yr CAGR is flattered by the FY2020 pandemic trough base. 3-yr CAGRs are negative because FY2022 was the fuel-surcharge peak.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip, net debt company). SBC is 0.3-0.5% of revenue throughout, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs barely differ; SBC is not where this valuation's risk lives. The FCF history is the story of capex intensity (18-20% of revenue since FY2023 vs 15% in FY2020-21) and East Palestine cash costs.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +5% (H1-2026 +5.9%, roughly half of it fuel surcharge) fading to 2.5% nominal; adjusted OR improves from ~66% toward ~61-62% over five years as PSR 2.0 / zero-based planning delivers about a point a year, then holds. Capex stays at railroad-normal 17-17.5% of revenue (D&A 11%), so the capex-over-D&A gap that defines rail FCF conversion persists. Cash tax ramps 15% -> 19% as bonus-depreciation deferrals partly reverse. Terminal: 16x owner FCF binds below Gordon (8.0% / 2.5%).

bull.narrative: Standalone best case, not the deal: intermodal truck-to-rail conversion and reshoring-led merchandise growth keep volume growth at 2-3% on top of 3% pricing; OR reaches CSX/UP-class ~59-60% (EBITDA margin 50%) by year 7; capex intensity eases to 16% as the post-derailment safety catch-up completes. 18x terminal cap reflects the scarcity value the market has paid for Class I networks.

bear.narrative: Deal is blocked or abandoned in 2027 after two years of strategic limbo: customer-contract and employee attrition, a mild industrial recession in 2027, coal decline and truck competition on intermodal hold volume flat; OR stalls at 67-68% (EBITDA margin ~44%); capex stays at 18.5% under heightened FRA/safety scrutiny; cash tax normalises to 21%. 14x terminal cap for a no-growth cyclical. Tax is never credited on a loss, EBIT stays positive throughout, and the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone NSC executes PSR 2.0 roughly as guided: revenue grows 3-4% nominal, adjusted operating ratio improves about a point a year from the mid-60s to the low-60s, capex stays at 17-17.5% of revenue. The three axes are (1) OR progression vs the mid-60s guidance, (2) intermodal and merchandise volume vs US industrial production, and (3) capex intensity, which is what separates rail EBITDA from rail FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Standalone upside: volume growth from truck conversion and reshoring, OR to the ~60% peer frontier, capex intensity easing toward 16%. This is the ceiling for NSC on its own; it is still ~30% below the UP consideration, which is why the deal, not operations, is the bull case the market is actually pricing.
scenario_narratives.bear: The STB blocks or conditions the merger into abandonment during 2027. NSC emerges with two years of deferred decisions, some customer and crew attrition, an industrial slowdown, and OR stuck near 67%. The stock loses the deal premium and re-rates toward standalone fundamentals; the ~$2.5B regulatory reverse termination fee (~$11/share, verify against the merger agreement) is the only cushion.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weight the STANDALONE scenarios; deal-completes vs deal-breaks is weighted separately in deal_overlay. Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the standalone future only becomes relevant if the deal fails, and a failed deal arrives with limbo damage (attrition, deferred capital decisions) that the base case does not carry. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (OR to ~60%, sustained volume growth, lower capex intensity) and NSC has trailed peers on OR execution for a decade.

deal_overlay.status: Pending acquisition by Union Pacific (announced 2025-07-29; NSC shareholders approved 2025-09; STB review ongoing, procedural schedule extended to late May 2027; BNSF, CSX, CPKC and shipper groups opposing).
deal_overlay.consideration: 1.0 UNP share + $88.82 cash per NSC share
deal_overlay.unp_price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close, Yahoo Finance chart API
deal_overlay.expected_close: Mid-2027 at the earliest given the STB schedule; ~9-12 months from the valuation date. NSC keeps paying its $1.35 quarterly dividend while pending.
deal_overlay.reverse_termination_fee: ~$2.5B payable by UNP to NSC on a regulatory failure (reported at announcement; verify against the merger agreement 8-K) = ~$11/share cushion in the break case.
deal_overlay.probability_rationale: A first-of-its-kind transcontinental Class I merger under the STB's 2001 'enhance competition' standard, with every other Class I and the main shipper associations on the record against it, a schedule already extended once, and a political environment that can change before mid-2027. Commitments offered (open gateways, rate protections) make an approval-with-conditions plausible, which is why this is 60% and not lower; it is not higher because the STB has never applied the 2001 rules to a transaction of this size.
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_method: 0.60 x 361.24 (consideration at UNP 272.42) + 0.40 x 170.61 (standalone weighted IV + termination fee) = 284.99. Consideration is NOT discounted for time because the $5.40/yr dividend collected while pending roughly offsets 9-12 months of carry at the cost of equity.
deal_overlay.market_implied_probability_note: (310.26 - 170.61) / (361.24 - 170.61) = 73% against the DCF break value; (310.26 - 245) / (361.24 - 245) = 56% against a pre-deal-band break value. The house 60% sits between the two: the price is consistent with the market both believing the deal is a modest favourite and refusing to mark NSC down to an owner-FCF value if it fails.
deal_overlay.break_value_note: Standalone weighted IV 159.61 + ~11 reverse termination fee. A market re-rate on a break would more likely land in the pre-announcement trading band (~$230-250, June 2025, ~20x earnings) than at the DCF value; both readings are given below.
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_value_if_break_rerates_not: 0.60 x 361.24 + 0.40 x 245 (midpoint of the pre-announcement band) = 314.74; this is roughly where the stock trades, i.e. the market is using a peer-multiple fallback, not an owner-FCF fallback.
deal_overlay.reading: At 310.26 the stock offers ~$51 (16%) of upside if the deal closes and ~$60-140 of downside if it breaks (to the pre-deal band or to the DCF band respectively). On the house 60% probability the expected value (~$285) is BELOW the price; on a peer-multiple fallback it is roughly AT the price. There is no margin of safety for a fundamental buyer at this level; this is a merger-arbitrage position whose return depends on the STB, not on NSC's cash flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Two valuations, kept apart on purpose. (1) The standalone owner-FCF DCF -- three scenarios, 10-year component build, 8.0% WACC, terminal capped at 14-18x owner FCF -- is the fundamental anchor: what NSC is worth as an eastern Class I railroad with 17-18% capex intensity and a mid-60s operating ratio. (2) The pending Union Pacific acquisition is the dominant near-term price driver and is handled as a deal overlay, not as a growth scenario: the consideration (1.0 UNP + $88.82) is a function of UNP's share price and STB approval odds, neither of which is a driver path. The market price sits between the standalone value and the consideration; where it sits is a statement about deal probability, not about NSC's cash flows. Deal completion caps upside at the consideration; a deal break re-rates the stock toward the standalone band, cushioned only by the reverse termination fee and the dividend collected while waiting.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_dcf_says: Standalone, the stock is worth materially less than the current price on every scenario, including the bull case. That is not unusual for a Class I railroad: the market pays 20-25x earnings for pricing power and network scarcity that an owner-FCF model, which charges the full 17-18% capex burden every year, does not credit. Pre-announcement (June 2025) NSC traded in the $230-250 range; the DCF range below that reflects the house 16x owner-FCF terminal cap and the full capex charge.
key_risks_to_valuation: STB outcome is binary and dominates the 12-month return: approval -> consideration (~$361 at UNP's current price, itself volatile); block/abandonment -> re-rate toward standalone, a 25-40% drawdown from the current price.
UNP share price: each $10 move in UNP moves the consideration $10/share; the stock component is unhedged for a plain holder.

Operating ratio execution: every point of OR is ~$120M of EBIT (~$0.45/share of earnings, ~$8-9/share of DCF value); the base case assumes ~4 points of improvement over five years that NSC has guided toward but not yet delivered on a full-year basis.
Capex intensity: the base case holds capex at 17-17.5% of revenue; a return to the 19-20% of FY2023-24 (safety catch-up) takes ~$15-20/share off the standalone value.
Cash tax rate: the model keeps cash tax below book (15% -> 19%) on permanent bonus depreciation; a legislative reversal would push the rate to 21% from year one, worth ~$8-10/share.
East Palestine tail: class settlement and insurance recoveries are largely closed, but residual litigation and FRA rule-making are ongoing; modelled as zero further cash cost.
Cyclicality: merchandise and intermodal volumes track US industrial production; a recession in the review window hits both the standalone value and, through UNP's price, the consideration.
